### Taxa Structure Overview (`Taxa`) {.topic-taxa}

The [VegVault]{.vegvault} database records the original [taxonomic names]{.taxa} derived directly from the [primary data sources]{.database}, and currently, it holds `r label_count(dplyr::pull(data_database_statistics, n_taxa))` [taxonomic names]{.taxa}.

```{r}
#| label: Taxa variables scheme structure
#| tbl-cap: "Column names and types for table `Taxa`."
data_comments_taxa <-
  tibble::tribble(
    ~column_name, ~description,
    "taxon_id", "ID of a Taxon (unique)",
    "taxon_name", "Name of a Taxon from primary source."
  )

load_db_table_data_types(
  con,
  "Taxa"
) %>%
  dplyr::full_join(
    data_comments_taxa,
    by = "column_name"
  ) %>%
  plot_table()
```

```{r}
#| label: Taxa scheme structure
build_absolute_graphics_include(
  here::here(
    "Outputs/Figures/website/DB_scheme_visualisation/Taxa.svg"
  )
)
```

### Sample-Taxa (`SampleTaxa`) {.topic-taxa}

Each individual [Taxon]{.taxa} is linked to corresponding [Samples]{.database} through the `SampleTaxa` table, ensuring accurate and systematic association between species and their ecological data. Note that the abundance information varies across the primary data sources. Therefore, users have to be careful while processing data from various sources. 

```{r}
#| label: SampleTaxa variables scheme structure
#| tbl-cap: "Column names and types for table SampleTaxa."
data_comments_sample_taxa <-
  tibble::tribble(
    ~column_name, ~description,
    "sample_id", "ID of a Sample",
    "taxon_id", "ID of a Taxon",
    "value", "Abundance representation of a Taxon (the units may differ among primary sources, i.e. Dataset Source-Types)"
  )
load_db_table_data_types(
  con,
  "SampleTaxa"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::full_join(
    data_comments_sample_taxa,
    by = "column_name"
  ) %>%
  plot_table()
```

```{r}
#| label: SampleTaxa scheme structure
build_absolute_graphics_include(
  here::here(
    "Outputs/Figures/website/DB_scheme_visualisation/SampleTaxa.svg"
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: Number of taxa per data source type
# The dataset type and source type of every dataset
data_dataset_types <-
  dplyr::inner_join(
    dplyr::tbl(con, "Datasets"),
    dplyr::tbl(con, "DatasetTypeID"),
    by = "dataset_type_id"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(
    dplyr::tbl(con, "DatasetSourceTypeID"),
    by = "data_source_type_id"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select("dataset_id", "dataset_type", "dataset_source_type")

# Taxa of plots and pollen samples are in SampleTaxa, taxa of trait records
#   in TraitsValue
n_taxa_per_source_type <-
  dplyr::union(
    data_dataset_types %>%
      dplyr::inner_join(
        dplyr::tbl(con, "DatasetSample"),
        by = "dataset_id"
      ) %>%
      dplyr::inner_join(
        dplyr::tbl(con, "SampleTaxa"),
        by = "sample_id"
      ) %>%
      dplyr::distinct(dataset_type, dataset_source_type, taxon_id),
    data_dataset_types %>%
      dplyr::inner_join(
        dplyr::tbl(con, "TraitsValue"),
        by = "dataset_id"
      ) %>%
      dplyr::distinct(dataset_type, dataset_source_type, taxon_id)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::count(dataset_type, dataset_source_type, name = "N") %>%
  dplyr::collect() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    dataset_type = stringr::str_replace_all(dataset_type, "_", " ")
  )

fig_n_taxa_per_source_type <-
  n_taxa_per_source_type %>%
  dplyr::arrange(-N) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    dataset_source_type = factor(
      dataset_source_type,
      levels = unique(dataset_source_type)
    )
  ) %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    ggplot2::aes(
      y = N,
      x = dataset_source_type
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    transform = scales::transform_log10(),
    breaks = c(10, 100, 1e3, 1e4, 1e5, 1e6),
    labels = scales::label_comma(),
    limits = c(10, 1e6)
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Taxa per source type, by dataset type",
    x = "",
    y = "Number of taxa"
  ) +
  ggplot2::guides(
    fill = "none"
  ) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~dataset_type, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  ggplot2::theme(
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "white")
  ) +
  # Colour marks the dataset type, as in every other figure
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values = palette_dataset_type
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      x = dataset_source_type,
      xend = dataset_source_type,
      yend = 0
    ),
    color = col_black
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      fill = dataset_type
    ),
    size = point_size,
    shape = 21,
    col = col_black
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_label(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      label = scales::label_comma()(N)
    ),
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = point_size * 2,
    family = font_family
  )

save_figure_to_render(fig_n_taxa_per_source_type)
```

### Taxon Classification (`TaxonClassification`) {.topic-taxa}

Each taxonomic name undergoes an automated classification (see [Database Assembly](database_assembly.qmd)) and results are stored in the `TaxonClassification` table. To classify the diverse taxa present in the [VegVault]{.vegvault} database, the {[taxospace](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/taxospace)} R package was used. This tool automatically aligns taxa names with the [Taxonomy Backbone](https://www.gbif.org/dataset/d7dddbf4-2cf0-4f39-9b2a-bb099caae36c) from the [Global Biodiversity Information Facility](https://www.gbif.org/), providing a standardized classification framework. Specifically, we try to find the best match of the raw names of taxa using the [Global Names Verifier](https://verifier.globalnames.org/).
Two kinds of names are corrected by hand after the automatic classification: fossil pollen types that combine two or more taxa, and the pollen type "Pinus Picea" (see [Database Assembly](database_assembly.qmd#i-taxonomic-classification)).

```{r}
#| label: TaxonClassification variables scheme structure
#| tbl-cap: "Column names and types for table `TaxonClassification`."
data_comments_taxon_classification <-
  tibble::tribble(
    ~column_name, ~description,
    "taxon_id", "ID of a Taxon",
    "taxon_species", "ID of a Taxon, which was assign as species level",
    "taxon_genus", "ID of a Taxon, which was assign as genus level",
    "taxon_family", "ID of a Taxon, which was assign as family level"
  )

load_db_table_data_types(
  con,
  "TaxonClassification"
) %>%
  dplyr::full_join(
    data_comments_taxon_classification,
    by = "column_name"
  ) %>%
  plot_table()
```


```{r}
#| label: TaxonClassification scheme structure
build_absolute_graphics_include(
  here::here(
    "Outputs/Figures/website/DB_scheme_visualisation/TaxonClassification.svg"
  )
)
```

Taxonomic classification for some [Taxa]{.taxa} might be only available down to the genus or family level, while most of the data is classified to species level.
Classification information, detailed up to the family level, is stored for each taxon, ensuring consistency and facilitating comparative analyses across different datasets.
Currently, the [VegVault]{.vegvault} database holds `r label_count(dplyr::pull(data_database_statistics, n_taxa))` taxonomic names, of which we were unable to classify only `r label_count(dplyr::pull(data_database_statistics, n_taxa_unclassified))` (`r label_share(dplyr::pull(data_database_statistics, n_taxa_unclassified) / dplyr::pull(data_database_statistics, n_taxa))`).

```{r}
#| label: taxa classification plot
# Total taxa, distinct species, genera and families, and taxa without any
#   classification, from the tested loader of the figures stage
n_taxa_per_class <-
  load_taxa_classification_counts(
    path_database = path_to_vegvault,
    list_build_manifest = list_build_manifest
  ) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    class = taxon_level,
    N = n_taxa
  )

# The levels count distinct names, so they do not add up to the total
vec_class_labels <-
  c(
    "total taxa" = "all taxa",
    "species" = "distinct species",
    "genus" = "distinct genera",
    "family" = "distinct families",
    "not classified" = "taxa not classified"
  )

fig_n_taxa_per_class <-
  n_taxa_per_class %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    class = factor(
      vec_class_labels[class],
      levels = vec_class_labels
    )
  ) %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    ggplot2::aes(
      y = N,
      x = class
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Taxa and their classification",
    x = "",
    y = "Number of names"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_comma(),
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      x = class,
      xend = class,
      yend = 0
    ),
    color = col_black,
    position = ggplot2::position_dodge(0.5)
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    size = point_size,
    shape = 21,
    col = col_black,
    fill = col_white,
    position = ggplot2::position_dodge(0.5)
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_label(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      label = scales::label_comma()(N)
    ),
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = point_size * 2,
    family = font_family,
    position = ggplot2::position_dodge(0.5)
  )

save_figure_to_render(fig_n_taxa_per_class)
```

### Taxon Reference (`TaxonReference`) {.topic-taxa}

Each taxon might get a reference. Currently, this is used to track the origin of the [Taxon]{.taxa} name (i.e. which primary source was used first with this [Taxon]{.taxa}). Note that [Taxa]{.taxa}, generated from taxonomic classification are associated with `taxospace` reference.

```{r}
#| label: TaxonReference variables scheme structure
#| tbl-cap: "Column names and types for table `TaxonReference`."
data_comments_taxon_reference <-
  tibble::tribble(
    ~column_name, ~description,
    "taxon_id", "ID of a Taxon",
    "reference_id", "ID of a Reference"
  )

load_db_table_data_types(
  con,
  "TaxonReference"
) %>%
  dplyr::full_join(
    data_comments_taxon_reference,
    by = "column_name"
  ) %>%
  plot_table()
```
